title: Centred smooth-section coordinates and their conormal monomials
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings), let $d\geq0$, and let $g:V\to S$ be smooth, separated and of finite type of pure relative dimension $d$, with a closed section $s:S\hookrightarrow V$, $g s=1_S$.
There is a Zariski open cover by affine $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i\subseteq S$ and affine open neighbourhoods $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i\subseteq V\times_SS_i$ containing $s(S_i)$, with separated etale $S_i$-maps $e_i:U_i\to\mathbf A^d_{S_i}$ carrying $s$ to zero, such that $e_i^{-1}(0)=s(S_i)$ scheme-theoretically. Writing $P_i=R_i[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$ and $J_i=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)$, the induced $P_i\to B_i$ is etale and flat, $I_i=J_iB_i$ is the section ideal, and $B_i/I_i=R_i$ by the section augmentation. The sequence of images of $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ is regular: multiplication by $x_j$ is injective modulo its predecessors. The empty sequence is allowed for $d=0$. Moreover, with $\mathcal I$ the ideal sheaf of $s(S)$ and $\mathcal E=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ regarded on $S$, $s$ is a regular immersion of codimension $d$, $\mathcal E$ is locally free of rank $d$, and the canonical multiplication map
$$\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}(\mathcal E)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{m\geq0}\mathcal I^m/\mathcal I^{m+1}$$
is an isomorphism. On each chart its degree-$m$ map sends a basis monomial in $[x_j]$ to the class of the same monomial in $I_i^m/I_i^{m+1}$; these identifications commute with restriction.
The scheme, morphism, algebra and coefficient notation and the specified comparison maps are those of [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-sbc-affine-space], [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].
Regular closed immersions of a specified codimension are as in [def-per-regular-closed-immersion-codimension], and base change is [def-pc-base-change].

proof.text: Fix $t\in S$. Apply [lem-sc-standard-smooth-local-relative-dimension] to $g$ at $s(t)$, using the given pure relative dimension $d$. Obtain affine opens $U_0\subseteq V$ and $T\subseteq S$ containing $s(t)$ and $t$, with $g(U_0)\subseteq T$, and a standard-smooth ring map of relative dimension $d$. Apply [lem-sc-standard-smooth-etale-polynomial-chart] to get an etale $T$-map $e_0:U_0\to\mathbf A^d_T$. The composite with projection is $g|_{U_0}$. This fixes the number of coordinates as the given $d$, rather than an unspecified local dimension.

The open $s^{-1}(U_0)\subseteq T$ contains $t$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], choose an affine open $T_1$ containing $t$ inside it. Replace $U_0$ by $U_1=U_0\times_TT_1$, which is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. The section now lands in $U_1$ on all of $T_1$. The base-changed chart is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. Write $a_j=s^*e_0^*x_j\in\Gamma(T_1,\mathcal O_{T_1})$. Compose the chart with the translation $x_j\mapsto x_j-a_j$ of affine space, whose inverse is $x_j\mapsto x_j+a_j$. Isomorphisms are open immersions, hence etale, and etale maps compose by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. We obtain an etale map $e:U_1\to\mathbf A^d_{T_1}$ with $es=0$. Since $U_1$ is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated] says that $e$ is separated.

source.place: Local construction, first sentence; affine refinements use Stacks 01IT/lemma-basis-affine-opens and 01I4/lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes

proof.text: Put $F=U_1\times_{\mathbf A^d_{T_1}}T_1$, where $T_1\to\mathbf A^d_{T_1}$ is zero. The map $F\to T_1$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] and separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change]. The equation $es=0$ gives a section $T_1\to F$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion]: this section identifies $T_1$ with an open and closed subscheme of $F$. Since $F\subseteq U_1$ is the closed subscheme cut out by the coordinate functions, the complementary subset $F\setminus s(T_1)$ is closed in $U_1$. Remove it, obtaining an open $W$ containing the section. Then $F\times_{U_1}W=s(T_1)$ as schemes, not just as sets: on the clopen section component the map to $T_1$ is the inverse isomorphism supplied by the cited section lemma.

source.place: Local construction, inverse image of zero, clopen section and removal of its complement; Stacks 024T/proposition-properties-sections

proof.text: Choose an affine open $W_0\subseteq W$ containing $s(t)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Choose an affine open $S_i\subseteq s^{-1}(W_0)\subseteq T_1$ containing $t$, by the same lemma. Set $U_i=W_0\times_{T_1}S_i$. This is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], is open in $V\times_SS_i$, and contains $s(S_i)$. The restricted map $e_i:U_i\to\mathbf A^d_{S_i}$ is etale by open-immersion composition and base change, using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]; it is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. The zero fibre remains exactly $s(S_i)$ by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Doing this for every $t$ gives the required Zariski cover. Each selected $S_i$ is nonempty. If $S$ is empty, take the empty cover. No intersection of two arbitrary affine opens has been assumed affine.

source.place: Tags 01IT/lemma-basis-affine-opens and 01I4/lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes; affine refinement of the blueprint Local construction

proof.text: Write $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$, $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ and $P_i=R_i[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$, $J_i=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], the chart ring map $P_i\to B_i$ is etale; it is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] the zero fibre has ring $B_i\otimes_{P_i}(P_i/J_i)=B_i/J_iB_i$: the explicit mutually inverse maps are $b\otimes\bar p\mapsto bp\bmod J_iB_i$ and $\bar b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Its identification with the section says exactly that the section augmentation $B_i\to R_i$ induces $B_i/J_iB_i\simeq R_i$. Consequently the section ideal is $I_i=J_iB_i$, also the affine ideal of [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf].

For $1\leq j\leq d$, the ring $Q_j=P_i/(x_1,\ldots,x_{j-1})$ is the polynomial ring $R_i[x_j,\ldots,x_d]$. Multiplication by $x_j$ on $Q_j$ is injective: it shifts the exponent of $x_j$ in each coefficient, so a product with zero coefficients has zero coefficients before shifting. Apply [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] over $P_i$, with flat module $B_i$, to this $P_i$-linear injection. Identify $B_i\otimes_{P_i}Q_j$ with $B_i/(x_1,\ldots,x_{j-1})B_i$ by $b\otimes\bar p\mapsto bp$ and $\bar b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Under these inverse maps the tensor injection is precisely multiplication by the image of $x_j$. Thus the coordinate list is weakly regular. Its final quotient is $R_i\ne0$, since $S_i$ contains $t$, so it is a regular sequence in the full convention [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. For $d=0$ the list is empty and the same final quotient argument applies.

source.place: Tag 00LF/definition-regular-sequence; flat preservation of injections, then the coordinate polynomial calculation

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial] to $B_i$ and the coordinate sequence of Step 6. Since $B_i/I_i=R_i$, it gives a graded isomorphism $R_i[T_1,\ldots,T_d]\simeq\operatorname{gr}_{I_i}(B_i)$ with $T_j\mapsto[x_j]_1$. Its degree-one clause says that $[x_1],\ldots,[x_d]$ is an $R_i$-basis of $I_i/I_i^2$; its degree-$m$ formula sends each monomial $T^\alpha$ to $[x^\alpha]_m$, and says these classes are an $R_i$-basis. The statement includes $m=0$ and the empty sequence.

Regard $U_i$ as an affine open of $V$ (the base $S_i\subseteq S$ is open). Its section kernel is generated by the length-$d$ regular list from Step 6. At every point of the section these are precisely the affine local equations required by [def-per-regular-closed-immersion-codimension]. Thus $s$ is a regular closed immersion of codimension $d$. The affine degree-one identification of [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra] identifies $\mathcal E|_{S_i}$ with the sheaf associated to $I_i/I_i^2$; applying [lem-sc-affine-conormal-frame] to the basis of Step 7 gives a free frame of length $d$. Hence $\mathcal E$ is locally free of rank $d$. For the empty source the local assertions are vacuous.

Use the canonical multiplication map $\psi:\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}(\mathcal E)\to\mathcal G$ specified by [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra]; both its affine identifications and its degree-one generator formula are part of that statement. The same node gives quasi-coherence of $\mathcal E=\mathcal G_1$, so [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-affine] identifies the source on $S_i$ with $\operatorname{Sym}_{R_i}(I_i/I_i^2)$. Use the basis of Step 7 and [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial] to identify this with $R_i[T_1,\ldots,T_d]$. The resulting map agrees with Step 7 on every $T_j$, hence agrees on all polynomials by addition and multiplication; it is therefore bijective on sections over $S_i$. Its formula on a degree-$m$ basis monomial is the asserted $[x^\alpha]_m$.

source.place: Tags 0631/equation-conormal-in-degree-n, 0632/equation-conormal-algebra-quotient, 0633/lemma-affine-conormal-sheaf; algebra.tex Tag 00LN and symmetric algebra Section 00DM

proof.text: The chartwise bijections of Step 9 are restrictions of the single map $\psi$. Explicitly restriction sends $[a_1]\cdots[a_m]$ to $[a_1|]\cdots[a_m|]=[(a_1\cdots a_m)|]$, since restriction is a ring homomorphism and preserves ideal powers. Thus the monomial descriptions commute with restriction, including on overlaps where the chosen coordinate bases differ. Both $\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}(\mathcal E)$ (by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-affine]) and $\mathcal G$ (by [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra]) are quasi-coherent, $\psi$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_S$-modules, and the affine opens $S_i$ cover $S$. Since $\psi$ is bijective on sections over every $S_i$ by Step 9, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-iso-on-affine-cover] shows that $\psi$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_S$-modules, hence of graded algebras, and so in every degree $m$. For $d=0$ one has $I_i=0$, so the graded algebra and symmetric algebra are both $R_i$ in degree zero and zero in positive degrees, with the displayed map the identity.
